newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Baloise taken to task over capitalisation.
newsitem.headline: Baloise taken to task over capitalisation.

text.p: Baloise Insurance Group deflected analysts' criticism that it is over-capitalised and said it is currently focusing on improving its returns.
"We are reworking the strategy. Our primary concern at the moment is operational improvements," said Michael Sundman, head of corporate development for Baloise, in a telephone interview with Reuters.

His comments followed publication of a study by Swiss equity analysts at CS Research dated October 1 which called Baloise "chronically overcapitalised." CS said the situation argued for the company to buy back its own shares, otherwise it risked an unfriendly takeover.
"A share buyback is the order of the day," CS said.
CS analyst Heinrich-Horst Wiemer said Switzerland's third-largest insurer should consider buying back shares held in large packages.

Wiemer, elaborating on the study, said tax reasons made such a strategy preferable to buying shares on the market. It should therefore consider buying stakes of roughly six percent held by Swiss Bank Corp and 6.7 percent owned by Baloise employee funds and pension funds.
According to CS, Baloise will likely have a book value of 3.2 billion Swiss francs, excluding minorities, at the end of 1996.

Regarding the ideal capitalisation for Baloise, CS said its low-risk business with the mass public argued for an optimal level of 2.5 to maximum 3.0 billion Swiss francs. CS urged a buyback of between 10 to 20 percent of Baloise's shares.
Even a buyback of 10 percent of its own shares would have an immediate impact on Baloise's earnings per share, and would also raise its return on equity (ROE), CS said.
With no share buyback, CS estimated Baloise's ROE at 6.38 percent. A 10 percent share buyback would raise its ROE to an estimated 6.64 percent, CS said.
Sundman also said Baloise's priority was its returns.
"As we have been telling the world, we are in the middle of a strategic planning process. Our primary concern now is with the return on investment.
"Our ROE is an important target for us, and we will be designing new management systems to help us meet that target," Sundman said.
He did not rule out that Baloise would also look more closely at its capitalisation at some point but did not say whether any changes might be made.
He said that while rating agencies should not be the primary focus of an insurer's business strategy, rating agencies also looked favourably on high capitalisation.
Baloise group net profit in the six months to June 30, 1996 rose to 109.1 million Swiss francs from 95.8 million in the comparable 1995 period.
Gross premiums totaled 4.2 billion francs compared with 4.12 billion in the same period.
Shareholders' equity was 3.1 billion.
Baloise registered shares traded 20 francs higher at 2,620 at midday Thursday.
